## Capture and restore

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| capture | Saving a warm workload so a later pod can start from it. Produces a checkpoint. |
| checkpoint | What a capture produces, named by a checkpoint id: CRIU images, the rootfs diff, replay mounts and, under gpushare, the chunk store; or, for a cachedir capture, the captured cache tree. |
| capture method | `cachedir` or `criu`, set for the whole cluster by the chart value `agent.captureMethod`. |
| cachedir capture | Captures the engine's model and compile caches into one directory (`/opt/nvsnap` in the pod); a restore mounts it read-only and the engine starts fresh against it. Also called rootfs capture in the code (`internal/rootfsonly`). |
| CRIU capture | Checkpoints the processes themselves with CRIU and the CUDA checkpoint API; a restore resumes them. |
| restore | Starting a pod from a checkpoint instead of cold. |
| cold start | A start with no checkpoint: download, load, compile. |
| placeholder | The pod a CRIU restore runs into: same spec as the captured pod, its main container waiting until the agent restores the captured processes into it. |
| rootfs diff | The captured container's writable layer, saved as `rootfs-diff.tar` and replayed into the placeholder before CRIU restores the processes. |
| replay mounts | The contents of `/dev/shm`, `/opt/nvsnap` and the pod's disk-backed emptyDir mounts, saved with the checkpoint and written back before restore; a memory-backed emptyDir is a tmpfs CRIU saves itself (`internal/agent/replay_mounts.go`). |
| gpushare | `libnvsnap_gpushare.so`, an `LD_PRELOAD` shim that releases GPU memory shared between processes before the CUDA checkpoint and re-creates it at the same addresses after; it is what makes multi-GPU CRIU capture possible. See [design/GPUSHARE.md](design/GPUSHARE.md). |
| chunk store | The node-local directory gpushare writes a process's GPU memory into, mounted at the same path at capture and restore. |
| node bundle | The binaries the agent stages on each node for other pods (CRIU, gpushare, the helper), versioned so an upgrade never replaces files a running pod uses. |

## Instances

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| instance | One serving unit that spans several pods, possibly on several nodes: a StatefulSet, LeaderWorkerSet or Grove group. Captured and restored as one group. |
| member | One pod of an instance. |
| rank | A member that holds GPUs; its ordinal is its place in the instance. |
| companion | A member without GPUs that the ranks talk to (an etcd, a NATS, a frontend), captured and restored with them. |
| group capture | Capturing every member of an instance together, opted in per instance. |
| group freeze | The point where every member of a group capture stops at once, so no member sees another stop before it. |

## Where bytes live: the tiers

A restore looks for a checkpoint in L1, L2 and L3, in that order, and takes
the first copy it finds (`internal/agent/cascade_fetch.go` `EnsureLocal`).
When the rails tier is on, it runs between L1 and L2. L4
is not in that order: replication fills it and pulls from it in the
background.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| L1 | The node's own copy, on its local disk. |
| L2 | Cluster storage: the per-checkpoint volume pair, or a shared filesystem when one is configured. |
| volume pair | The `rwx-<hash>` volume a capture is written to and the `rox-<hash>` read-only volume restores mount, made from it by promotion. |
| promotion | Turning a written `rwx-` volume into its read-only `rox-` twin (by snapshot or by a shared read-only attach, depending on storage). |
| L3 | Peer fetch: another agent that holds the checkpoint sends it over HTTP; every node that restores becomes a peer. |
| rails tier | Opt-in fetch between L1 and L2: bedrock-peer copies the checkpoint from nodes that hold it over the nodes' RDMA NICs, in pods that claim the NICs through DRA only for the copy. |
| L4 | An object-store bucket shared between clusters (cross-cluster replication of cachedir captures, `internal/agent/replication.go`). |

## Models and caches

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| model volume | One volume per model per cluster, downloaded once and read by every pod that runs the model (`internal/modelvolume`). |
| identity | The model a pod will download, as a URI (`hf://`, `ngc://`, `s3://`, `nim://`), decided at admission (`internal/modelid`). |
| landing | Where a pod finds the model volume: the path the engine already reads, mounted from the volume. |
| primary | The volume a model or cache set is written to; readers mount read-only views of it. |
| cache set | The compile caches of one configuration, every rank's in one volume. Not used under CRIU capture. |
| election | Choosing one pod to download (and capture) per hash when a chart starts many workers at once, by creating a Lease (`internal/election`). The winner is the leader; the others are followers and wait. Not used under CRIU capture. |
| hash | The content identity of a capture: what it runs and on what GPU architecture. |

## Admission and the platform

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| webhook | The mutating admission webhook, served by the agent, that prepares pods for capture or restore. |
| inject scope | Which namespaces the webhook covers: `all` (every namespace not labelled `nvsnap.io/inject=false`) or `optIn` (only namespaces labelled `nvsnap.io/inject=true`). |
| opt-in | How an instance is chosen for group capture: the pod annotation `nvsnap.io/criu-capture: "true"`, or the chart value `agent.criuCaptureOptIn` for pods nvsnap does not author. |
| NVCA | The NVIDIA Cloud Functions cluster agent, which deploys functions and calls nvsnap to capture and restore them. |

## Retired words

| Word | Use instead |
|---|---|
| cryo, gpucr | nvsnap (former names) |
| L1/L2/L3 as transport legs (intra-cluster, object storage, cross-cluster), as in the transport proposal | the tiers above |
| blobstore, nvsnap-blobstore | L4 (the object store) |
| warm cold-start | cachedir capture and restore |
| rootfs-only path | cachedir capture |
